items.experiments_react_native: **Experiments.** Tree of Life, Image Agent and Factory Arm, live at $t(links.experiments), with code at $t(links.github).
items.factory_architecture: **$t(common:experiment_factory_arm).** A browser simulation of a robot arm unloading a pallet. One WebSocket per page carries protobuf frames, chosen over gRPC-Web for bidirectional streaming. A Rust bridge relays them to a digital twin in NVIDIA Isaac Sim and answers “hold still” when it’s unreachable. Each session gets its own simulated rig, and the GPU machine stops itself when idle.
items.factory_arm: **$t(common:experiment_factory_arm).** A browser-based robotic palletisation experiment. Planning runs in web workers, while a Rust bridge relays Protobuf frames over WebSocket to a digital twin running in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
items.image_architecture: **$t(common:experiment_image_agent).** A public prompt-to-image agent with a fixed workflow. Every request passes four checks, cheapest first, and quotas are counted in MongoDB so a restart does not reset them. A reply cut short by a restart is marked failed when the conversation is next opened, so nobody is locked out.
items.image_frontend_ai: **$t(common:experiment_image_agent).** A public prompt-to-image agent, built to learn what it takes to put an AI feature in front of real people. A clarifier asks one question at a time, up to three, and code enforces the limit. The workflow is fixed in code as well, so the model never chooses its own tools. A vision model reviews each picture and can trigger one retry. Every request passes four checks, cheapest first: rate limits, rule checks, moderation and a small classifier. Quotas are counted in MongoDB, and progress arrives over a GraphQL subscription.
items.image_master: **$t(common:experiment_image_agent).** A public prompt-to-image agent that asks up to three clarifying questions, reviews generated images with a second model, and applies rate limits, rule checks, moderation and classification.
items.interpreter_react_native: **Interpreter (prototype).** A speech interpreter for two-way conversation. The Expo app (React Native, Tamagui) records push-to-talk audio and sends each utterance over a WebSocket to a Fastify server. The server detects the speaker's language, translates with Claude using the conversation so far, and streams captions back. The phone then speaks the result on-device. 21 languages, including Cantonese and Mandarin.
items.ki_architecture: **$t(projects.labels.ki).** A React host loads design-system, API-client and experiment remotes at runtime. The GraphQL API (Apollo Server, MongoDB) sits behind a same-origin proxy that injects server-issued keys. Production runs on Google Cloud Run.
items.ki_frontend_ai: **$t(projects.labels.ki).** The federated platform under all of these. A React host loads a design-system remote and a typed GraphQL client at runtime, and production runs on Google Cloud Run.
items.ki_master: **$t(projects.labels.ki).** My personal platform, built as a federated architecture. A React host loads a design-system remote and typed GraphQL client at runtime, backed by Apollo Server and MongoDB. Deployed on Google Cloud Run.
items.ki_react_native: **$t(projects.labels.ki).** My personal platform, built as a federated architecture. A React host loads a design-system remote and typed GraphQL client at runtime. Deployed on Google Cloud Run.
items.tree_architecture: **$t(common:experiment_tree_of_life).** The Open Tree of Life’s 2.3 million species, cached in MongoDB as a parent-pointer tree with idempotent upserts, since lineages that share ancestors are written at once. Illustrations are generated in the background and arrive over a GraphQL subscription. Text, image and vision calls each fail over across providers, with timeouts and cooldowns.
items.tree_frontend_ai: **$t(common:experiment_tree_of_life).** A walk through the Open Tree of Life’s 2.3 million species, cached in MongoDB as a parent-pointer tree. Illustrations are generated on demand by a fixed pipeline: resolve the lineage, pick a species, write the prompt, generate, score with a vision model, retry once. Text, image and vision calls each have their own provider failover chain, with timeouts and cooldowns.
items.tree_master: **$t(common:experiment_tree_of_life).** An interactive exploration of the Open Tree of Life’s 2.3 million species. Each organism’s illustration is generated on demand through a fixed AI pipeline with provider failover and vision-model review.
items.writing_frontend_ai: **Writing reviewer** (code only: $t(links.moonshot)). Reviews commit messages, pull-request descriptions and READMEs with Claude. The model returns structured edits, each tied to a named rule. Code locates every quote and drops any edit that does not match exactly. It turns away prompt-injection attempts and has an eval set.
